item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WATCH - SEVERE THUNDERSTORM - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Severe Thunderstorm/Lightning Warning | Yellow Watch - Severe Thunderstorm - In Effect |

A cold front associated with an intensifying low pressure system will combine with an unseasonably warm and unstable atmosphere creating favourable conditions for the development of severe thunderstorms. Thunderstorms are currently ongoing over the region and will continue to increase in coverage over the area and eventually develop into a line and move eastward toward the Manitoba border later this afternoon. Thunderstorms will also gradually intensify early this afternoon. The primary hazards with these thunderstorms will be strong wind gusts of 90-100 km/h, large hail, and heavy rainfall. Brief tornadoes are also possible with intense thunderstorms. The severe weather threat will diminish once the cold front pushes eastward into Manitoba later this evening. Driving conditions may be difficult. Damage to roofs, fences, branches or soft shelters is possible. Heavy rain can cause flash flooding and significant reductions to visibility. Strong wind gusts can damage trees, buildings and overturn vehicles. Severe thunderstorm watches are issued when conditions are favourable for the development of thunderstorms capable of producing damaging hail, wind or rain. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using MBStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Expected - act within an hour | Kenton, Manitoba

item.title: BE ALERT - YELLOW WARNING - RAINFALL - IN EFFECT
item.description:
Generic Warning | Yellow Warning - Rainfall - In Effect |

Heavy rain is expected. Heavy rain associated with a low pressure system is expected to begin in southern Saskatchewan this afternoon. Rain will continue through to Monday evening. Rainfall totals are expected to be 50 to 60 mm. Locally higher amounts up to 80 to 100 mm are possible in thunderstorms. Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Some travel delays are possible. Local utility outages are possible. Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using SKStorm.

| Moderate - possible threat | Future - act in near future | Yorkton, Saskatchewan

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
